public_rationale: The token concern holds for input encoding: the same text can require more tokens. The broader comparison does not hold consistently. Artificial Analysis measured higher aggregate performance with about 35% fewer output tokens, while a smaller coding evaluation found equal test pass rates. Higher input-token counts therefore support one part, but do not show generally worse performance or greater total token consumption.
limitations: Benchmark results do not rule out regressions in particular user workflows.
The independent aggregate comparison used maximum effort.
Stet tested one repository with 28 tasks; its page was updated May 1, while the reported runs occurred April 16.
The outcome depends on distinguishing input-token inflation from complete-task consumption.

criteria.support_condition: Comparable evaluations show poorer task performance and greater token consumption. Evidence limited to one task class or token category supports only that part.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evaluations show equal or better task performance or lower token consumption. Opposing results across the two parts or across token categories warrant a mixed assessment.
